content.title: About
content.content: The McDonalds Hamburger is a classic fast‑food item consisting of a grilled beef patty, bun, slice of cheese, pickles, onions and a special sauce. It originated in the 1940s in the United States and has become one of the most recognizable dishes of the chain.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first McDonalds hamburger was sold in 1948 at the brothers' restaurant in California.
Since 1975 the menu has featured the signature "Special Sauce", a closely guarded recipe.
McDonalds sells over 75 million hamburgers worldwide each year.
Ingredient composition varies by country; for example, India uses a chicken patty instead of beef.
The hamburger is frequently highlighted in promotional campaigns, including limited‑edition sauces.

items.title: Protein
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Red meat is a good source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The burger contains vitamin B12 and niacin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, important for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Energy density
items.content: Its high calorie content provides a quick energy boost, useful during periods of increased physical activity.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Frequent consumption can contribute to weight gain and elevated cholesterol levels.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Salt in the bun and sauce raises sodium intake, which may affect blood pressure.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Contains milk, gluten, and sometimes soy, making it a potential allergen.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Some regions include preservatives that may cause sensitivity in certain individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The hamburger is typically eaten by hand, holding the bottom bun. It can be paired with fries, sauce, and a drink. For a healthier option, replace the beef patty with chicken or a plant‑based alternative.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Freshly prepared burgers should be consumed immediately. Leftovers can be stored in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours, then reheated to an internal temperature of 75 °C.
